title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional (SAP-C02)
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the AWS SAP-C02 exam guide (the five official domains and their weightings). Not a capture of past exam questions.
source_label: AWS Solutions Architect Professional practice bank

items.stem: A global enterprise wants to guarantee that no developer can launch resources in AWS Regions outside its approved set, regardless of the IAM permissions their role grants. The company needs a preventive control that applies to every account under a single organizational unit. Which solution should a solutions architect recommend?
options: Create a service control policy that denies actions unless aws:RequestedRegion matches the approved Regions, and attach it to the organizational unit
Attach an IAM permissions boundary to every developer role listing the approved Regions
Deploy an AWS Config rule in each account that flags non-compliant resource creation
Enable a CloudTrail trail in each account and review the logs for out-of-Region activity
items.explanation: A service control policy at the organizational unit level sets the maximum permissions for every principal in those accounts and is evaluated before IAM, so a Region condition denies out-of-Region calls organization-wide. IAM permission boundaries apply only to the principals they are attached to and do not stop account administrators creating other roles, an AWS Config rule detects violations after the fact rather than preventing them, and CloudTrail only records activity without blocking anything.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A company runs more than eighty VPCs across several accounts and needs them to communicate with each other and with an on-premises data center through a single managed hub. Connectivity must scale without a full mesh and must route between the on-premises network and every VPC. Which service should the solutions architect use?
options: Private hosted zones shared through every VPC peering connection
AWS Transit Gateway with VPC attachments and a Direct Connect gateway
A full mesh of VPC peering connections between every pair of VPCs
A software VPN appliance running on a large EC2 instance in each VPC
items.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway is a regional hub that attaches many VPCs and on-premises connections and routes between them, avoiding a full mesh. VPC peering is non-transitive, so eighty VPCs would need thousands of peering links and still could not reach on-premises through a peer, a per-VPC VPN appliance is unmanaged and creates overlapping routing, and shared private hosted zones provide name resolution only, not connectivity.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A regulated company is creating a new multi-account AWS environment with a landing zone. It wants automated account provisioning with pre-configured guardrails, centralized logging, and a dashboard that reports account baseline compliance. Which offering provides all of these from a managed baseline?
options: AWS Organizations alone with a manual tagging convention
AWS Service Catalog portfolios replicated by hand to every account
AWS Control Tower with Account Factory and guardrails
A set of hand-built CloudFormation StackSets run manually in each organizational unit
items.explanation: Control Tower provides an opinionated landing zone, Account Factory for automated provisioning, preventive and detective guardrails, and a compliance dashboard. Manually run StackSets and hand-replicated portfolios lack the managed baseline and automated account provisioning, while Organizations alone gives account grouping and billing but no landing-zone guardrails or baseline reporting.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A company central security account must assume a role in each workload account to read a compliance S3 bucket. The workload accounts are owned by different teams, and the security team cannot store long-term keys. Which approach enforces least privilege and avoids sharing secrets?
options: Generate an IAM user access key in each workload account and distribute the keys to the security team
Share the workload accounts root user credentials with a shared password vault
Configure the bucket to allow public read access so any principal can retrieve objects
Create an IAM role in each workload account that trusts the security account principal and grant the security team permission to assume it
items.explanation: Cross-account role assumption uses short-lived STS credentials and a trust policy naming the security account, so no long-term secret is distributed and permissions stay scoped. Long-lived access keys in shared distribution violate least privilege and are hard to rotate, sharing root credentials is unsafe and unauditable, and public read exposes compliance data to the Internet.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A company wants every CloudTrail event from all accounts in its organization to flow into one dedicated logging account and to be tamper-resistant. Which combination meets the requirement with the least operational effort?
options: Create an organization trail in the management account that delivers to an S3 bucket in the logging account with a bucket policy scoped to the organization
Configure an individual trail in each account and email the log files to the logging team each day
Enable CloudTrail in the management account only and assume it captures member account events
Store CloudTrail logs in each account own bucket and rely on account owners to retain them
items.explanation: An organization trail automatically applies to all accounts and delivers to a central bucket, and a bucket policy scoped by aws:PrincipalOrgID lets only the organization write there, which resists tampering by member accounts. Per-account trails with email are manual and incomplete, a management-account trail records only that account, and per-account local buckets let an owner delete or modify the evidence.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A company has many AWS accounts and wants to simplify billing and receive volume discounts across all of them. Each account must keep its own AWS Identity and Access Management boundaries. Which action achieves this?
options: Enable a billing transfer in each account IAM policy without joining an organization
Create an AWS organization and add the accounts as members to consolidate billing while keeping separate accounts
Merge every workload into one account and use IAM users to separate the teams
Create a separate payer account for billing and keep workloads in unrelated standalone accounts
items.explanation: Adding accounts to an AWS organization consolidates their usage for volume pricing and a single bill while each account retains its own IAM boundary and resource isolation. Merging into one account destroys the security boundary between teams, standalone accounts linked only for billing cannot share committed-use discounts the same way, and billing is not controlled by an IAM policy.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: Several application accounts must share a common set of subnets in a central VPC so their resources communicate with low latency while a network team retains control of the subnet layout. Which feature should the solutions architect use?
options: A Transit Gateway attachment that shares the subnet route tables
AWS PrivateLink endpoints published by each application account for the others
AWS Resource Access Manager to share the VPC subnets with the participant accounts
VPC peering between each application account VPC and the central VPC
items.explanation: VPC sharing through AWS Resource Access Manager lets participant accounts launch resources directly into subnets owned by the central account, giving a shared network with low-latency east-west traffic while the owner controls subnets. Peering keeps separate subnets and does not share them, Transit Gateway connects VPCs but not their subnets, and PrivateLink exposes specific services rather than shared subnets.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A company needs resources in many VPCs to resolve names in a single private hosted zone that the network team manages centrally, without copying records. Which design delivers centralized private DNS resolution?
options: Create a separate private hosted zone in every VPC and synchronize records with a script
Use public hosted zones and rely on split-horizon DNS behavior
Resolve the names through the on-premises DNS servers only
Create the private hosted zone in the network account and associate it with the VPCs, using Route 53 Resolver rules for forwarding
items.explanation: A private hosted zone in a central account can be associated with multiple VPCs so all of them resolve the same records, and Route 53 Resolver outbound and inbound endpoints plus rules handle hybrid forwarding. Duplicated zones with scripts drift, public zones expose records and are not the private resolution mechanism, and relying only on on-premises DNS leaves AWS-only lookups unresolved.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A company has a single AWS Direct Connect connection at one location and wants to reach VPCs in three Regions, including VPCs created later in accounts it does not yet know. Which component lets one private virtual interface reach many VPCs across Regions?
options: AWS Direct Connect gateway linked to virtual private gateways or Transit Gateways in each Region
A separate dedicated Direct Connect connection for every VPC in each Region
A public virtual interface that routes to each VPC public endpoints
An AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the Internet in place of Direct Connect
items.explanation: A Direct Connect gateway is a global object that can be associated with virtual private gateways or Transit Gateways in multiple Regions over a single connection and virtual interface. Provisioning a connection per VPC is costly and slow, a public virtual interface reaches public services rather than private VPC addressing, and a VPN over the Internet is not the dedicated Direct Connect path.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A company wants employees to sign in once and access many AWS accounts with permissions defined by their group, without creating IAM users in each account. Which service should the solutions architect implement?
options: AWS Certificate Manager issuing client certificates to employees
AWS IAM Identity Center with permission sets assigned to groups and accounts
Federated IAM users created manually in every account
A shared IAM role in each account with the same credentials for all staff
items.explanation: IAM Identity Center provides single sign-on to multiple accounts and assigns permissions through permission sets and group assignments. Manually created IAM users multiply administrative work and lack central identity, a shared role gives no per-user accountability, and ACM issues TLS certificates and does not manage workforce access.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A security team attaches a service control policy to an organizational unit. A developer IAM policy in a member account allows the S3 CreateBucket action, but the service control policy does not mention S3. What happens when the developer tries to create a bucket?
options: The action fails because service control policies remove all permissions by default
The action is allowed only after the service control policy is detached
The action is allowed because the service control policy does not deny it and the IAM policy permits it
The action is denied because the service control policy does not explicitly allow it
items.explanation: Service control policies filter permissions but do not grant them, and an action is allowed when the policy does not restrict it and the principal IAM policy permits it. Service control policies are not allow-lists that deny unmentioned actions, so options claiming implicit denial or total removal are wrong, and detaching the policy is unnecessary.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A company must enforce the same AWS WAF rules, security groups, and Shield protections across accounts in its organization, including new accounts added automatically. Which service centralizes this?
options: A CloudFormation template that each account owner deploys on request
AWS Config rules that report non-compliant accounts to management
Amazon GuardDuty findings forwarded by email to each account
AWS Firewall Manager with an organization-wide policy
items.explanation: Firewall Manager applies and continuously enforces WAF, security group, and Shield policies across an organization, including newly added accounts. Per-account templates depend on owners and drift, AWS Config is detective rather than preventive central management, and GuardDuty detects threats but does not configure protection policies.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A company is designing its organizational units so production accounts inherit stricter guardrails than sandbox accounts. Which design principle should guide the organizational unit structure?
options: Group accounts by policy needs such as environment or function so service control policies attached to the unit apply the right controls
Place every account in a single flat organizational unit to keep policies simple
Group accounts by the surname of the account owner to ease administration
Group accounts by AWS Region so each Region has its own policy
items.explanation: Organizational units exist to apply differentiated policies, so grouping by environment or function lets stricter service control policies cover production and looser ones cover sandboxes. A flat unit cannot differentiate guardrails, and owner-name and Region groupings do not align with policy needs and complicate inheritance.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A hybrid environment requires that on-premises servers resolve AWS private hosted zone names and that AWS resources resolve on-premises names. Which two-way DNS design should be recommended?
options: AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a two-way trust and no resolver endpoints
Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoints for on-premises queries and outbound endpoints with forwarding rules for on-premises names
A single outbound endpoint with static routes added to the VPC route table
Public hosted zones that both AWS and on-premises servers query directly
items.explanation: Inbound Resolver endpoints let on-premises resolvers query Route 53, and outbound endpoints with rules forward AWS queries to on-premises resolvers, giving two-way hybrid resolution. Route table changes do not forward DNS, public zones do not hold private records, and a directory trust alone does not provide general DNS forwarding for all names.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A network team builds a central Transit Gateway and wants to let several application accounts attach their VPCs without giving them ownership of the Transit Gateway. Which approach allows sharing?
options: Give every application account full administrator access to the network account
Distribute the Transit Gateway private key to each application team
Share the Transit Gateway with Resource Access Manager and let accounts create their own attachments
Create a Transit Gateway in each application account and peer them together
items.explanation: Resource Access Manager shares the Transit Gateway so participant accounts can create and manage their own VPC attachments while the owner retains control of the gateway. Duplicating gateways loses the single hub, granting administrator access violates least privilege, and a Transit Gateway has no private key to distribute.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A financial company must ensure all Amazon EC2 instances are tagged with a cost-center value before they are created, and wants a preventive organization-wide control. Which solution should be used?
options: A tag policy that only reports missing tags to the finance team
A Lambda function that runs hourly to stop untagged instances
An S3 bucket policy that denies access to untagged resources
A service control policy that denies ec2:RunInstances when the request lacks a cost-center tag
items.explanation: A service control policy can conditionally deny ec2:RunInstances when the cost-center request tag is missing, which prevents creation up front. A tag policy standardizes tag keys and values but does not block creation, an hourly Lambda reacts after the resource exists, and an S3 bucket policy governs S3 access and cannot control EC2 creation.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A company wants all outbound Internet traffic from dozens of VPCs to pass through a single inspected egress path in a shared services VPC. VPCs must not each deploy their own NAT gateways. Which design meets this goal?
options: Route egress through a central NAT gateway in the shared services VPC reached over a Transit Gateway, with inspection applied in the path
Deploy a NAT gateway in every VPC and remove the shared services account
Give each VPC an Internet gateway and place an Elastic IP on every instance
Use only VPC peering so traffic bypasses the central account
items.explanation: Centralizing egress through one NAT gateway in a shared services VPC reached over Transit Gateway reduces redundant gateways and creates one inspection point. NAT gateways in every VPC defeat centralization and raise cost, giving every instance a public IP exposes instances directly, and peering bypasses the inspected central path.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity

items.stem: A team is building containerized microservices with highly variable, bursty demand and wants to avoid managing servers or clusters. The workload runs on Linux containers and needs rapid scaling. Which compute option is most appropriate?
options: Amazon EMR clusters running the containers
AWS Fargate tasks launched by Amazon ECS
A large Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances running the containers
AWS Lambda functions packaged as container images but limited to fifteen-minute runs
items.explanation: Fargate runs containers without managing servers or clusters and scales tasks without a node fleet, which suits bursty Linux workloads. Managing an EC2 Auto Scaling group reintroduces node operations, Lambda caps execution duration and is not ideal for long-running services, and EMR is a big-data service rather than a general container platform.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A serverless API must handle a predictable daily traffic spike that currently causes cold-start latency, while keeping costs low between spikes. Which configuration should the solutions architect recommend for the functions?
options: Move the function into a VPC with a NAT gateway
Set the function timeout to the maximum of fifteen minutes
Configure provisioned concurrency on the Lambda alias for the spike window
Increase the function memory to the maximum value to reduce cold starts
items.explanation: Provisioned concurrency keeps execution environments initialized so requests avoid cold starts during known spikes, and it can be scheduled for the spike window only to control cost. Maximum memory raises per-invocation cost without removing initialization, placing a function in a VPC does not reduce cold starts and can add latency and NAT cost, and a longer timeout does not affect startup latency.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A production relational database must survive the loss of an entire Availability Zone with minimal disruption, and the company wants automatic failover without changing the connection string. Which Amazon RDS configuration meets this?
options: A single-AZ instance with a daily snapshot copy to another Region
A read replica in the same Availability Zone used as the failover target
An EC2 instance running a self-managed database with an Elastic IP
A Multi-AZ deployment with a standby replica and a DNS endpoint that fails over automatically
items.explanation: RDS Multi-AZ maintains a synchronous standby in another Availability Zone and fails over automatically by repointing the instance endpoint. A single-AZ instance cannot survive an Availability Zone loss in real time, a same-AZ read replica shares the failure domain and is not automatic failover, and a self-managed database requires manual recovery and public addressing.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A company needs a relational database with an active-passive cross-Region disaster recovery strategy and a recovery point objective near one second. Which solution best fits?
options: Amazon Aurora Global Database with a secondary Region cluster
Amazon RDS for MySQL with nightly cross-Region snapshot copies
A read replica in a single Region and manual promotion
A self-managed MySQL cluster synchronized with rsync
items.explanation: Aurora Global Database replicates with about one-second latency and allows promoting a secondary Region within minutes, meeting the near-one-second recovery point objective. Nightly snapshots give a recovery point objective of up to a day, a same-Region read replica does not protect against a Regional failure, and rsync file synchronization is not a database replication strategy.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A globally distributed application needs a key-value store that remains writable in multiple Regions simultaneously and reconciles concurrent writes. Which service feature should be used?
options: Amazon Redshift clusters synchronized across Regions
Amazon DynamoDB global tables in an active-active configuration
A single-Region DynamoDB table with cross-Region read replicas configured manually
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with logical replication to each Region
items.explanation: DynamoDB global tables provide fully managed multi-Region, active-active replication with last-writer-wins conflict resolution. Manual cross-Region read replicas are not an active-active multimaster feature, RDS logical replication is operationally heavy and not globally active-active by default, and Redshift is a data warehouse rather than a low-latency key-value store.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A company stores millions of objects with unpredictable and changing access patterns and wants to minimize storage cost automatically without retrieval penalties. Which S3 configuration should be recommended?
options: S3 One Zone-IA for every object
A lifecycle rule that deletes objects after thirty days
S3 Intelligent-Tiering on the bucket
S3 Standard for all objects indefinitely
items.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors access and moves objects between tiers automatically with no retrieval fees, which fits unpredictable patterns. S3 Standard never optimizes cost, One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone and has a minimum duration, and deleting objects after thirty days risks data loss and is not cost optimization of retained data.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: An order system must deliver each event to several independent consumer services, and each consumer must receive every event even if it is briefly unavailable. Which design decouples the producer from many consumers?
options: Publish to a single Amazon SQS queue that all consumers poll
Write events to a file in Amazon S3 that each consumer polls
Send events directly to each consumer with retries in the producer code
Publish to an Amazon SNS topic with an Amazon SQS queue subscribed for each consumer
items.explanation: The SNS fanout pattern with one SQS queue per consumer gives every consumer its own durable copy so a slow consumer does not block others. A single shared queue lets one consumer steal another messages, S3 polling is not event delivery and adds latency, and direct calls with producer-side retries tightly couple services and fail when a consumer is down.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A streaming analytics pipeline must process events in the exact order they were produced for each customer while scaling horizontally. Which design preserves per-customer ordering?
options: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and set the customer identifier as the partition key
Use a single shard for the entire stream to guarantee a global order
Use Amazon SQS standard queues with many consumers
Use Amazon SNS topics and let consumers sort events after receiving them
items.explanation: Kinesis preserves order within a shard, so using the customer identifier as the partition key keeps each customer events ordered while multiple shards scale the stream. A single shard limits throughput and scales only vertically, SQS standard queues do not guarantee order, and SNS does not retain messages for later sorting.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A payment service needs exactly-once processing and must silently discard duplicate messages produced by retries. Which queue type should be used?
options: An Amazon MQ broker using automatic acknowledgment
An Amazon SQS FIFO queue with content-based deduplication
An Amazon SQS standard queue with a high visibility timeout
An Amazon SNS topic with HTTP subscriptions
items.explanation: SQS FIFO queues provide deduplication and single delivery per message group, so repeated sends of the same content are dropped. Standard queues are at-least-once and can duplicate, SNS does not provide deduplication of consumed messages, and Amazon MQ automatic acknowledgment does not deduplicate producer retries.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A company serves private videos from an S3 bucket through CloudFront and must prevent users from bypassing CloudFront to fetch objects directly from S3. Which configuration restricts access?
options: Restrict access with a set of IP addresses on the bucket
Encrypt the objects with an SSE-KMS key and share the key publicly
Use an Origin Access Control so CloudFront signs requests and the bucket policy allows only that distribution
Make the bucket public and rely on CloudFront caching to hide the origin
items.explanation: Origin Access Control lets CloudFront sign requests to S3, and a bucket policy that allows only the distribution denies direct access. A public bucket exposes objects, IP restrictions are brittle because CloudFront edge addresses change, and sharing a KMS key does not restrict the S3 data plane or stop direct downloads.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A public API on API Gateway experiences bursts that could overwhelm the backend, and the company wants to protect the backend and apply fair limits per client. Which feature should be configured?
options: A larger backend instance and no gateway throttling
CloudFront only, with no API Gateway throttling
An S3 bucket policy limiting request rate
Usage plans with API keys and per-method throttling limits
items.explanation: API Gateway usage plans with API keys and throttling enforce per-client request rates and protect the backend. Simply scaling the backend does not prevent overload or enforce fairness, CloudFront caching does not throttle API calls or identify clients, and an S3 bucket policy cannot rate-limit API Gateway.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A web application stores session state in the application server local memory, which breaks when instances scale behind a load balancer. Which change fixes the session persistence problem?
options: Move the session state to an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster
Enable sticky sessions on the load balancer and never scale down
Store sessions in an instance store volume on one server
Increase the instance size so it can hold all sessions
items.explanation: An ElastiCache for Redis cluster externalizes session state so any instance can serve any user and scaling keeps sessions. Sticky sessions reduce availability and still lose sessions when an instance fails, instance store is ephemeral and tied to one host, and a larger instance raises cost without solving shared state.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A company wants a stateless web tier to fail over between two Regions automatically if the primary Region is unhealthy. Which combination delivers Regional failover with health-based routing?
options: Static DNS records pointing to one Region with a long TTL
Route 53 failover routing with health checks pointing to a secondary Region endpoint
A single Region deployment with a larger Auto Scaling group
An Elastic Load Balancer in one Region only
items.explanation: Route 53 failover routing with health checks directs traffic to the secondary Region when the primary fails its health check. A single-Region Auto Scaling group cannot survive a Regional outage, one load balancer is bound to its Region, and static DNS with a long TTL cannot detect failure or redirect promptly.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A workload has a repeating weekly demand pattern, and the operations team wants the capacity to be ready before traffic rises while still responding to unexpected spikes. Which Auto Scaling approach fits best?
options: Use only simple scaling with a five-minute cooldown
Disable scaling and keep a fixed fleet sized for peak
Use predictive scaling for the weekly pattern and target tracking for unexpected spikes
Use only a scheduled action that scales up once a week
items.explanation: Predictive scaling learns recurring patterns and pre-provisions capacity, while target tracking reacts to unexpected load, so combining them covers both cases. A single weekly scheduled action misses spikes, simple scaling reacts late and can oscillate, and a fixed peak-sized fleet wastes money during troughs.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A machine learning team needs a shared, high-throughput POSIX file system that many Linux instances can mount at the same time and that grows automatically. Which storage should be recommended?
options: A single Amazon EBS volume attached to all instances at once
Amazon S3 mounted with a third-party gateway on every instance
An instance store volume replicated by the application
Amazon EFS with multiple mount targets across Availability Zones
items.explanation: Amazon EFS is a shared, elastic NFS file system that many Linux instances mount concurrently and that scales with usage. A standard EBS volume attaches to one instance per Availability Zone, S3 is object storage without native POSIX semantics, and instance store is local and ephemeral.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A Lambda function connects to an Amazon RDS database, and bursts of invocation are exhausting database connections. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?
options: Use Amazon RDS Proxy to pool and reuse database connections
Increase the database maximum connections and hope for the best
Open a new connection inside every function invocation and close it after
Move the database credentials into environment variables to speed connections
items.explanation: RDS Proxy maintains a managed connection pool that Lambda functions share, preventing connection exhaustion. Raising the connection limit can overload the database, opening a connection per invocation is exactly what causes exhaustion, and storing credentials in environment variables improves secret handling but not connection pressure.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Design for New Solutions

items.stem: A company runs steady-state Amazon EC2 and AWS Lambda workloads and wants to reduce compute cost with a commitment while preserving flexibility across instance families and Regions. Which purchasing option is most flexible?
options: Spot Instances for the steady-state production tier
AWS Compute Savings Plans covering the committed hourly spend
Standard Reserved Instances locked to one instance family in one Region
On-Demand Instances only, with no commitment
items.explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply across instance families, sizes, Regions, and Lambda usage, giving discounts with flexibility. Standard Reserved Instances lock to a specific family and Region, On-Demand gives no discount, and Spot Instances can be interrupted and are unsuitable for steady production tiers.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions

items.stem: A company stores billions of log objects. Only the most recent thirty days are queried frequently, older data is rarely read but must be retained for seven years at the lowest cost. Which approach optimizes cost?
options: Delete objects after thirty days to save storage
Copy all objects to Amazon EBS volumes for faster access
An S3 lifecycle policy that transitions objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after the active period
Keep every object in S3 Standard for the full seven years
items.explanation: A lifecycle policy moving rarely accessed objects to Glacier Deep Archive minimizes storage cost while satisfying the seven-year retention. Keeping everything in S3 Standard pays the highest rate, deleting after thirty days violates retention, and EBS is far more expensive per gigabyte and not designed for cold archives.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions

items.stem: A company suspects many EC2 instances are over-provisioned. Which service recommends rightsizing based on observed utilization and is free to use?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor business support checks only
Amazon CloudWatch dashboards reviewed manually
AWS Cost Explorer tag report
AWS Compute Optimizer
items.explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes utilization metrics and recommends rightsizing for EC2, Auto Scaling groups, and other resources. Trusted Advisor has some checks but does not provide per-instance rightsizing recommendations, manual dashboard review is not automated guidance, and Cost Explorer reports spend but not instance sizing.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions

items.stem: A production Amazon RDS instance runs continuously at a stable size and the company wants the largest discount for it. Which choice most reduces cost for this steady database?
options: Purchase Reserved Instances for the RDS instance class and Region
Convert the database to a smaller burstable instance to cut cost
Take a snapshot every hour and restore from it on demand
Move the database to S3 to avoid instance charges
items.explanation: Reserved Instances give a significant discount for steady-state RDS usage in a specific class and Region. Downsizing may not meet performance needs and is a resize decision rather than a pricing one, frequent snapshots add storage cost without reducing instance cost, and moving a relational database to S3 changes the workload and is not equivalent.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions

items.stem: A cost review finds many unattached EBS volumes and idle load balancers left from past projects. Which practice directly removes this waste?
options: Buy more Reserved Instances to absorb the extra usage
Identify and delete unused resources with a tagging and lifecycle review process
Increase the size of the remaining volumes so they are less likely to fill
Move the idle load balancers to another Region instead of deleting them
items.explanation: Regularly reviewing tags and deleting unattached volumes and idle load balancers removes ongoing waste. Enlarging volumes increases cost, moving idle resources keeps paying for them, and buying reservations for unused capacity locks in spend rather than eliminating it.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions

items.stem: An application latency occasionally spikes and the team cannot correlate requests across microservices. Which combination provides distributed tracing and request-level insight?
options: AWS CloudTrail management events for every API call
Amazon Macie scanning the application logs
AWS X-Ray with tracing enabled on the services and the SDK instrumented
Amazon CloudWatch Logs alone with no trace identifiers
items.explanation: X-Ray instruments requests across services to build a service map and trace segments, which reveals where latency occurs. Plain CloudWatch logs lack correlation across services, CloudTrail records AWS API calls rather than application request paths, and Macie is a data-classification service for S3.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions

items.stem: A read-heavy web application is overloading its relational database and most queries return the same popular records. Which change reduces database load with the least application rewrite?
options: Shard the database across many instances
Move the database to a larger instance and do nothing else
Convert all reads to a nightly batch job
Add an Amazon ElastiCache layer in front of the database for popular reads
items.explanation: A cache absorbs repeated reads for popular records, cutting database load with minimal code changes. Sharding is a large architectural change, scaling up helps only until the next ceiling, and batching reads to nightly is not viable for an interactive web application.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions

items.stem: A company wants to prove that its multi-tier application survives an Availability Zone failure. Which practice provides the most confidence in resilience?
options: Run controlled failure injection and game days that simulate an Availability Zone outage
Review the architecture diagram with the team once a quarter
Assume the Multi-AZ configuration guarantees recovery and skip testing
Document a manual recovery runbook and never exercise it
items.explanation: Deliberate failure injection and game days validate that failover actually works and surface hidden dependencies. Diagrams and assumptions do not test behavior, and an unexercised runbook may be stale and fail under real pressure.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions

items.stem: A company deploys infrastructure by hand and experiences configuration drift between environments. Which operational change improves reliability and repeatability?
options: Snapshot production and copy it to development once a year
Define infrastructure as code in CloudFormation or Terraform and deploy through a pipeline
Continue manual changes but keep a detailed wiki of the steps
Give each engineer their own AWS account and manual process
items.explanation: Infrastructure as code makes environments reproducible, reviewable, and free of drift by deploying through version control and pipelines. A wiki documents manual steps but does not remove drift, per-engineer manual accounts increase inconsistency, and yearly snapshots cannot keep environments in sync.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions

items.stem: Users worldwide report slow page loads from a web application hosted in one Region. Static assets and API responses repeat across users. Which change improves global latency most directly?
options: Increase the database read capacity in the same Region
Add more application servers behind the existing load balancer
Distribute content with Amazon CloudFront and cache static and cacheable responses at edge locations
Move the application to a larger instance in the same Region
items.explanation: CloudFront serves cached content from edge locations close to users, reducing round-trip latency for global audiences. A larger instance, more read capacity, and more servers all remain in one Region and do not shorten the distance to users.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions

items.stem: A company pays high data-processing charges because private subnets route traffic to AWS services through a NAT gateway. Which change reduces this cost while keeping traffic private?
options: Send the traffic over the public Internet instead of the NAT gateway
Move the workloads into public subnets to avoid the NAT gateway
Compress the traffic before it leaves the subnet
Create gateway VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB and route that traffic directly
items.explanation: Gateway VPC endpoints route S3 and DynamoDB traffic privately without NAT gateway processing charges. Sending traffic over the Internet is not private and may not be cheaper, public subnets expose resources, and compression does not remove NAT data-processing charges.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions

items.stem: A security review finds that production EC2 instances have unpatched operating systems and no continuous vulnerability assessment. Which AWS service continuously scans instances for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure?
options: Amazon Inspector
AWS CloudTrail
AWS Config
Amazon GuardDuty
items.explanation: Amazon Inspector continuously scans EC2 instances, container images, and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. CloudTrail records API activity, AWS Config evaluates configuration compliance, and GuardDuty detects threats such as compromised credentials but does not perform vulnerability scanning.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions

items.stem: A company must migrate hundreds of on-premises physical and virtual servers to AWS with minimal application changes and minimal downtime. Which service is purpose-built for this rehost?
options: AWS DataSync
AWS Application Migration Service
AWS Database Migration Service
AWS Snowball Edge
items.explanation: AWS Application Migration Service continuously replicates source servers and launches them on AWS with minimal downtime and no application changes, which is the rehost pattern. Database Migration Service moves databases rather than whole servers, Snowball transfers data offline, and DataSync moves file data rather than running servers.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization

items.stem: A company has fifty terabytes of data in a remote data center with limited and slow network bandwidth, and the migration must finish within a few weeks. Which transfer method is most practical?
options: AWS Transfer Family with SFTP over the Internet
A nightly rsync job over a VPN for the next year
AWS Snowball Edge devices shipped to the data center for offline transfer
AWS DataSync over the existing Internet connection
items.explanation: Snowball Edge physically moves large volumes of data when network bandwidth is too limited to finish in time. DataSync, Transfer Family, and rsync all depend on the same constrained network and would take far longer than the migration window.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization

items.stem: A company will migrate an Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and must convert schemas, stored procedures, and data. Which combination should be used?
options: AWS Database Migration Service alone to both convert and migrate everything
A manual export to CSV files loaded with the AWS CLI
AWS Application Migration Service to lift the Oracle server as an EC2 instance
AWS Schema Conversion Tool to convert the schema and AWS Database Migration Service to move and replicate the data
items.explanation: The Schema Conversion Tool converts heterogeneous schemas and code, and Database Migration Service performs the data migration and ongoing replication. Database Migration Service moves data but does not convert proprietary schema objects, CSV exports lose procedures and are error-prone, and rehosting the Oracle server is not a database migration to Aurora.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization

items.stem: A company must cut over from an on-premises database to Amazon Aurora with only a short maintenance window and almost no data loss. Which migration approach minimizes downtime?
options: Use AWS Database Migration Service with ongoing replication and cut over once the target is caught up
Take a full logical dump and restore it during the maintenance window
Copy the database files to S3 and import them in the window
Stop the application for a full week while the data is copied
items.explanation: Database Migration Service performs a full load and then continuous change data capture, so the target stays current and the cutover is only as long as the final catch-up. One-time dumps require the whole copy inside the window, S3 file copies are not a live replication path, and a week-long outage is unacceptable.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization

items.stem: A company wants to move its legacy application to AWS while replacing only its self-managed message broker with a managed service and leaving the application code otherwise intact. Which migration strategy does this describe?
options: Repurchase, moving to a completely different SaaS product
Replatform, making a few targeted changes to gain managed benefits
Refactor, completely re-architecting the application before migration
Retire, decommissioning the application without replacement
items.explanation: Replatform keeps the core application but swaps selected components for managed services, which matches replacing only the broker. Refactor rewrites the architecture, retire removes the application, and repurchase replaces it with a different product.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization

items.stem: A company wants to rehost applications but is concerned about keeping operating-system and application licenses compliant after the move. Which aspect of AWS Application Migration Service helps?
options: It replaces every operating system with Amazon Linux during migration
It removes the need for any licensing because AWS instances are license-free
It replicates the source server so existing licensing arrangements can continue on the migrated instance
It automatically converts all commercial licenses to open-source equivalents
items.explanation: Because Application Migration Service replicates the server as-is, existing licensing can continue on the matching AWS instance. It does not convert or substitute licenses, it does not replace the operating system, and AWS instances still require valid licenses for commercial software.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization

items.stem: A company must copy millions of files from an on-premises NFS server to Amazon EFS and keep them synchronized for a period. Which service is designed for this file data movement?
options: AWS Snowcone shipped to the data center
AWS Database Migration Service
Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose
AWS DataSync with a scheduled task
items.explanation: AWS DataSync moves and synchronizes file data over the network between on-premises storage and AWS file services such as EFS and S3. Snowcone is used when the network is unsuitable, Database Migration Service moves databases, and Firehose streams data into destinations but does not sync file systems.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization

items.stem: An enterprise wants to migrate a mainframe batch workload to AWS and reduce reliance on the mainframe over time. Which service accelerates moving mainframe applications and data to AWS?
options: AWS Mainframe Modernization
AWS Application Migration Service for Linux servers
Amazon EMR for Hadoop workloads
AWS Glue for ETL pipelines
items.explanation: AWS Mainframe Modernization provides tools and runtime environments to rehost or replatform mainframe workloads. Application Migration Service targets standard servers, EMR is a big-data processing service, and Glue is a managed ETL service, none of which address mainframe workloads.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization

items.stem: A company running VMware vSphere on-premises wants to extend its existing data centers into AWS with the same operational tooling during a gradual migration. Which service supports this hybrid model?
options: Amazon WorkSpaces for all server workloads
VMware Cloud on AWS
Amazon EC2 bare-metal instances used as standalone hypervisors
AWS Outposts rack only, without vSphere
items.explanation: VMware Cloud on AWS runs the VMware software-defined data center on AWS and connects to on-premises vSphere environments using the same tools. Bare-metal instances are not a managed VMware environment, Outposts extends AWS to your site but is not the VMware-managed service, and WorkSpaces is a desktop service rather than a server platform.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization

items.stem: A company wants to modernize a monolithic application incrementally by routing some features to new microservices while the rest of the monolith keeps running. Which pattern supports this approach?
options: Lift and shift, moving the monolith unchanged to EC2 and stopping there
Retire the monolith immediately and rebuild from scratch in one sprint
Strangler Fig, placing new services in front of the monolith and migrating features gradually
Big-bang rewrite, replacing the monolith in a single release
items.explanation: The Strangler Fig pattern introduces new services gradually behind a routing layer and shifts functionality over time, lowering risk. A big-bang rewrite concentrates risk, a pure lift and shift does not modernize, and an immediate rebuild in one sprint is unrealistic and risky.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization

items.stem: An application in one account must encrypt data with a customer managed KMS key in a central security account and allow automated access without changing the key policy. Which mechanism grants cross-account decryption to specific principals with the least privilege?
options: Making the KMS key policy use the wildcard principal for all accounts
Copies of the key exported to each application account as plaintext
Embedding the key material in the application environment variables
A KMS grant issued to the application role that allows the required encrypt and decrypt operations
items.explanation: KMS grants delegate specific operations to particular principals without editing the key policy, which supports temporary, least-privilege cross-account use. A wildcard principal grants access too broadly, KMS symmetric key material cannot be exported as plaintext, and embedding key material is an insecure anti-pattern.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Security

items.stem: A company wants centralized workforce access where permissions for each team are defined once and assigned to many accounts, and it wants the permission definitions version-controlled. Which IAM Identity Center feature defines these permission bundles?
options: Permission sets that are assigned to groups for each account
IAM users created separately in each account
IAM roles named after each individual employee
AWS Config rules that enforce a permission baseline
items.explanation: Permission sets in IAM Identity Center are reusable definitions of policies that can be assigned to groups across accounts and managed as code. Per-account IAM users do not centralize identity, per-employee roles multiply maintenance, and Config rules assess compliance but do not grant identity permissions.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Security

items.stem: An application uses an Amazon RDS database password stored in a configuration file. The company wants automatic rotation and retrieval through API calls at run time. Which service should be used?
options: A hard-coded password in the container image
AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation of the database secret
An encrypted Amazon S3 object that the application downloads at startup
A parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store without rotation
items.explanation: Secrets Manager stores, retrieves, and automatically rotates database credentials through API calls so no secret is embedded in code. An S3 object does not rotate and requires managing access separately, a plain Parameter Store value lacks built-in rotation, and hard-coding secrets in an image is insecure and static.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Security

items.stem: A security team wants an automated response when Amazon GuardDuty reports that an EC2 instance is communicating with a known malicious host. Which design enables automatic remediation?
options: Store the finding in Amazon S3 and review it during the next audit
Disable GuardDuty after the first finding to reduce noise
Send the GuardDuty finding to Amazon EventBridge with a rule that invokes a Lambda function to isolate the instance
Email the finding to the security distribution list for manual handling
items.explanation: GuardDuty findings are events that EventBridge can match to invoke a Lambda function that applies a quarantine security group or stops the instance. Email and periodic review are manual and slow, and disabling GuardDuty removes detection entirely.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Security

items.stem: A company wants continuous vulnerability assessment for its container images stored in Amazon ECR and its EC2 fleet. Which service provides this scanning?
options: Amazon Macie
AWS Shield Advanced
AWS CloudHSM
Amazon Inspector
items.explanation: Amazon Inspector scans ECR images, EC2 instances, and Lambda functions for vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. Macie discovers sensitive data in S3, Shield Advanced protects against DDoS, and CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware key storage, none of which scan for vulnerabilities.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Security

items.stem: A company must discover and classify personally identifiable information stored in Amazon S3 buckets across many accounts. Which service should the solutions architect use?
options: Amazon Macie
Amazon Inspector
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon GuardDuty
items.explanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning to discover and classify sensitive data such as personally identifiable information in S3. Inspector scans compute for vulnerabilities, CloudTrail logs API activity, and GuardDuty detects threats, none of which classify S3 data.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Security

items.stem: A company collects security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, and third-party tools and wants one normalized view with the ability to route findings by account. Which service aggregates them?
options: Amazon Detective
AWS Security Hub
AWS Config
AWS Trusted Advisor
items.explanation: Security Hub aggregates and normalizes findings from AWS services and partner tools into a single dashboard with organization-wide views. AWS Config evaluates resource configuration, Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks, and Detective supports investigation but does not aggregate and normalize findings.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Security

items.stem: A company must retain a record of all AWS API activity across accounts and capture accepted and rejected traffic at the network interface for a forensic investigation. Which two data sources should be enabled?
options: Amazon GuardDuty for API activity and AWS Trusted Advisor for network traffic
AWS Artifact for API activity and Amazon Inspector for network traffic
AWS CloudTrail for API activity and VPC Flow Logs for network traffic
AWS Config for API activity and Amazon Macie for network traffic
items.explanation: CloudTrail records API calls and VPC Flow Logs capture IP traffic metadata at the elastic network interface. Config, GuardDuty, and Artifact serve different purposes, and Macie, Trusted Advisor, and Inspector do not produce VPC traffic logs.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Security

items.stem: A company terminates TLS for its public website at an Application Load Balancer and wants managed certificate issuance and automatic renewal for the domain. Which service should be used?
options: A self-signed certificate generated on each web server
An SSH key pair generated in EC2
AWS CloudHSM storing the web server private key
AWS Certificate Manager with a certificate attached to the load balancer
items.explanation: AWS Certificate Manager issues public certificates for integrated services and renews them automatically. Self-signed certificates trigger browser warnings and require manual renewal, SSH keys are for host access rather than TLS, and CloudHSM stores keys but does not issue or renew certificates.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Security

items.stem: A security team wants to identify which IAM roles and resource policies grant external access to its resources so it can remove unintended sharing. Which service should be used?
options: IAM Access Analyzer
AWS CloudTrail Insights
Amazon Inspector
AWS Firewall Manager
items.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer analyzes resource policies and role trust policies to identify resources shared with external principals. CloudTrail Insights detects unusual API activity, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, and Firewall Manager centrally manages protection policies, none of which find external access grants.
items.reference: AWS SAP-C02 Exam Guide - Security
